newsitem.title: UK: World oil prices slide as oversupply pressures.
newsitem.headline: World oil prices slide as oversupply pressures.

text.p: World oil prices slid further on Thursday, continuing a three-day slump that has cut more than a dollar off the value of a barrel of crude.
Benchmark Brent crude oil futures for July delivery closed at $18.32, 40 cents down on Wednesday's close, with prices heading towards the $17.80-$18.30 range seen in April, this year's low point.
Brent was trading on Monday above $19.50 before the market weakened as evidence of oversupply mounted and the institutional futures buyers who have propped up the market took fright and sold out.
"The fund money that was long has been shaken out of the market and bearish fundamentals have once more come to the fore," said Leslie Nicholas, at brokers GNI.
Two sets of U.S. oil data released this week, although contradictory in parts, painted a picture of rising crude and petroleum product stocks, despite torrid refinery throughput.
The confirmation that the United Nations would renew its deal allowing Iraq to sell crude oil under the "oil-for-food" plan added to the impression of ample supply and weak demand, traders said.
"Once sentiment switched the sell-off just built up a momentum of its own," said Nicholas.

Crude sellers are now looking for support from a pick-up in gasoline demand in the United States -- the key summer market for the product -- and some indication of production restraint when OPEC members meet in Vienna on June 25th.
Gasoline prices have not yet risen as expected in North America at the start of the traditional "driving season" when vacationers fuel up their vehicles.

Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries curtailed their production in May by only 100,000 barrels per day (bpd), despite calls from OPEC bosses to respect much-flouted quota limits, according to a Reuters survey.

Wellhead crude production fell to 26.95 million bpd, still well above the 11 nation OPEC "ceiling" of 25.03 million bpd, largely because of maintenance rather than voluntary restraint, the survey found.
Many traders are sceptical the Vienna meeting will be able to halt the hectic rate of over-production which has helped push prices down from the $20 plus range of last year.

More immediately traders are waiting for the latest monthly survey of oil market trends by the International Energy Agency, the West's oil watchdog, due out on Friday. Crude oil prices in dollars per barrel:
